extracted.intended_audience: registrants (public companies) and their technical, legal, and financial advisors preparing SEC filings regarding oil, gas, and mining operations
extracted.subtask_description: Regulation S-K disclosure requirements and definitions for oil & gas and mining registrants, including required items, definitions of technical terms, qualified person/reporting rules, and instructions on presentation and supporting documentation for public filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party report contents (reserves)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a registrant files a third-party report regarding reserves, the report must include (among other items) a discussion of the possible effects of regulation on the ability of the registrant to recover the estimated reserves; a discussion regarding the inherent uncertainties of reserves estimates; a statement that the third party has used all methods and procedures as it considered necessary under the circumstances to prepare the report; a brief summary of the third party's conclusions with respect to the reserves estimates; and the signature of the third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items (e.g., discussion of regulatory effects, uncertainties, methodology statement, summary conclusions, signature) are required components of the third-party report submitted under Item 1202.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserves audit — scope and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of Item 1202, a 'reserves audit' means the process of reviewing certain of the pertinent facts interpreted and assumptions underlying a reserves estimate prepared by another party and rendering an opinion about the appropriateness of the methodologies employed, the adequacy and quality of the data relied upon, the depth and thoroughness of the reserves estimation process, the classification of reserves appropriate to the relevant definitions used, and the reasonableness of the estimated reserves quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reserves audit is an evaluative process focused on methods, data quality, classification consistency, and reasonableness of quantities; auditors should document opinion elements accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserves sensitivity analysis (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant may, but is not required to, provide a reserves sensitivity analysis showing sensitivity of proved/probable/possible reserves to different price scenarios by principal product type in tabular format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If provided, the registrant may disclose estimates by product type based on different price and cost criteria (e.g., ranges, standardized futures prices, management forecasts) and must disclose the price and cost schedules and assumptions on which the disclosed values are based. A sample table format is provided (Sensitivity of Reserves to Prices by Principal Product Type and Price Scenario).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on disclosure of non-reserve resource estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates of oil or gas resources other than reserves, and any estimated values of such resources, shall not be disclosed in any document publicly filed with the Commission, unless such information is required to be disclosed in the document by foreign or state law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: where such estimates previously have been provided to a party offering to acquire/merge/consolidate with the registrant (or affiliates) in connection with that acquisition, such estimates may be included in documents related to the acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proved undeveloped reserves — total quantity at year end
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the total quantity of proved undeveloped reserves at year end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 1203(a) requires a year-end aggregate disclosure of proved undeveloped reserves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proved undeveloped reserves — material changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose material changes in proved undeveloped reserves that occurred during the year, including proved undeveloped reserves converted into proved developed reserves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 1203(b) requires registrants to report material increases/decreases and conversions during the fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proved undeveloped reserves — investments and progress to convert
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss investments and progress made during the year to convert proved undeveloped reserves to proved developed reserves, including, but not limited to, capital expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 1203(c) expects narrative about actions and spending aimed at development of PUDs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proved undeveloped reserves — explanation of long-term undeveloped reserves
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the reasons why material amounts of proved undeveloped reserves in individual fields or countries remain undeveloped for five years or more after disclosure as proved undeveloped reserves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 1203(d) requires explanation for PUDs remaining undeveloped for five-plus years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production disclosure — volumes by product, geography, and material fields
rubrics_metrics.description: For each of the last three fiscal years disclose production, by final product sold, of oil, gas, and other products. Disclosure shall be made by geographical area and for each country and field that contains 15% or more of the registrant's total proved reserves expressed on an oil-equivalent-barrels basis unless prohibited by the country in which the reserves are located.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 1204(a) establishes a three-year history requirement with geographic and material-field breakdowns; follow foreign-law exceptions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average sales price and average production cost disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: For each of the last three fiscal years disclose, by geographical area: (1) the average sales price (including transfers) per unit of oil, gas and other products produced; and (2) the average production cost, not including ad valorem and severance taxes, per unit of production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 1204(b) requires both price and cost per-unit metrics for the same three-year period and geographic breakdown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net production definition and guidance (Instruction 1 to Item 1204)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, net production should include only production that is owned by the registrant and produced to its interest, less royalties and production due others. In special situations (e.g., foreign production) net production before any royalties may be provided, if more appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'net before royalty' figures are furnished, the registrant must note the change from the usage of 'net production'. Use the definition that best reflects the registrant's situation and disclose any deviation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gas production inclusion/exclusion rules (Instruction 2 to Item 1204)
rubrics_metrics.description: Production of natural gas should include only marketable production of natural gas on an 'as sold' basis. Include dry, residue, and wet gas depending on whether liquids have been extracted before transfer of title. Omit flared gas, injected gas, and gas consumed in operations. Recovered gas-lift gas and reproduced gas should not be included until sold. Synthetic gas, when marketed as such, should be included in natural gas sales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 1204 Instruction 2 clarifies which gas volumes count as production for disclosure and which do not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate disclosure for products sold prior to conversion (Instruction 3 to Item 1204)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any product, such as bitumen, is sold or custody is transferred prior to conversion to synthetic oil or gas, the product's production, transfer prices, and production costs should be disclosed separately from all other products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid aggregating pre-conversion products with converted products; provide separate lines and metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer price determination standard (Instruction 4 to Item 1204)
rubrics_metrics.description: The transfer price of oil and gas (natural and synthetic) produced should be determined in accordance with FASB ASC paragraph 932-235-50-24 (Extractive Activities—Oil and Gas Topic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the cited FASB ASC guidance when computing transfer price for internal transfers and disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of average production cost and units (Instruction 5 to Item 1204)
rubrics_metrics.description: The average production cost, not including ad valorem and severance taxes, per unit of production should be computed using production costs disclosed pursuant to FASB ASC Topic 932, Extractive Activities—Oil and Gas. Units of production should be expressed in common units of production with oil, gas, and other products converted to a common unit of measure on the basis used in computing amortization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the same basis for unit conversion as used for amortization computations and follow ASC Topic 932 for cost definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drilling disclosure — number of wells drilled (Item 1205(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each of the last three fiscal years, by geographical area, disclose: (1) the number of net productive and dry exploratory wells drilled; and (2) the number of net productive and dry development wells drilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a three-year, geography-specific breakdown separating exploratory vs development wells and productive vs dry, using defined terms for net/counting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — dry well
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'dry well' is an exploratory, development, or extension well that proves to be incapable of producing either oil or gas in sufficient quantities to justify completion as an oil or gas well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition when classifying wells for Item 1205 reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — productive well
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'productive well' is an exploratory, development, or extension well that is not a dry well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any well not fitting the 'dry well' definition should be classified as productive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion refers to installation of permanent equipment for production of oil or gas, or, in the case of a dry well, to reporting to the appropriate authority that the well has been abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion status is the basis for counting and reporting wells drilled/completed during the fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — number of wells drilled
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of wells drilled refers to the number of wells completed at any time during the fiscal year, regardless of when drilling was initiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count wells completed during the fiscal year even if drilling started earlier; count multiple completions in same bore hole as one well (see Item 1208 gross well guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of other exploratory or development activities (Item 1205(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose, by geographic area, for each of the last three years, any other exploratory or development activities conducted, including implementation of mining methods for purposes of oil and gas producing activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include non-well activities of material importance by geography for the three-year period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present activities disclosure (Item 1206)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose, by geographical area, the registrant's present activities, such as the number of wells in the process of being drilled (including wells temporarily suspended), waterfloods in process of being installed, pressure maintenance operations, and any other related activities of material importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the description of present activities as of a date at the end of the most recent fiscal year or as close to the filing date as reasonably possible. Include only wells in the process of being drilled at the 'as of' date and express them in terms of both gross and net wells. Do not include wells that the registrant plans to drill but has not commenced unless material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery commitments — material disclosure (Item 1207(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant is committed to provide a fixed and determinable quantity of oil or gas in the near future under existing contracts or agreements, disclose material information concerning the estimated availability of oil and gas from any principal sources, including: (1) the principal sources and total amounts expected from each and all sources combined; (2) the total quantities subject to delivery commitments; and (3) steps taken to ensure available reserves and supplies are sufficient to meet such commitments for the next one to three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 1207 requires forward-looking disclosure about sources, quantities, and mitigation steps for delivery commitments for a 1–3 year horizon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery commitments — presentation and factors to consider (Item 1207(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the information required in a form understandable to investors and based upon facts and circumstances including disclosure by geographic area; significant supplies dedicated or contracted to the registrant; any significant reserves or supplies subject to priorities or curtailments affecting certain customers; priority allocations or price limitations imposed by regulatory agencies; other factors beyond control (e.g., third-party control of drilling, competition, availability of foreign reserves); and any impact on earnings and financing needs resulting from inability to meet contractual obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor the disclosure to investor understanding and to the registrant's specific circumstances, addressing regulatory, contractual, and marketplace constraints and financial impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery commitments — past failures disclosure (Item 1207(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant has been unable to meet any significant delivery commitments in the last three years, describe the circumstances concerning such events and their impact on the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide narrative explanation and effects on operations/finances for any significant missed commitments during the preceding three years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — available reserves (Item 1207(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of Item 1207, 'available reserves' are estimates of the amounts of oil and gas which the registrant can produce from current proved developed reserves using presently installed equipment under existing economic and operating conditions and an estimate of amounts that others can deliver to the registrant under long-term contracts or agreements on a per-day, per-month, or per-year basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition when assessing reserve availability to meet delivery commitments; include both produced and contractually deliverable volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oil and gas properties, wells, operations, acreage — gross/net productive wells and developed acreage (Item 1208(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose, as of a reasonably current date or as of the end of the fiscal year, the total gross and net productive wells, expressed separately for oil and gas (including synthetic oil and gas produced through wells) and the total gross and net developed acreage (i.e., acreage assignable to productive wells) by geographic area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide current or year-end counts of gross/net productive wells and developed acreage, broken out by geography and by oil vs gas (including synthetic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oil and gas properties — undeveloped acreage disclosure (Item 1208(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose, as of a reasonably current date or as of the end of the fiscal year, the amount of undeveloped acreage, both leases and concessions, if any, expressed in both gross and net acres by geographic area, together with an indication of acreage concentrations, and, if material, the minimum remaining terms of leases and concessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report undeveloped acreage gross/net by geography, note concentration and remaining lease terms when material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — gross well or acre
rubrics_metrics.description: A gross well or acre is a well or acre in which the registrant owns a working interest. The number of gross wells is the total number of wells in which the registrant owns a working interest. Count one or more completions in the same bore hole as one well. In a footnote, disclose the number of wells with multiple completions. If one of the multiple completions in a well is an oil completion, classify the well as an oil well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gross counting for wells/acreage where the registrant has any working interest; disclose multiple completions in footnote and classify by completion type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — net well or acre
rubrics_metrics.description: A net well or acre is deemed to exist when the sum of fractional ownership working interests in gross wells or acres equals one. The number of net wells or acres is the sum of the fractional working interests owned in gross wells or acres expressed as whole numbers and fractions of whole numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute net counts by summing fractional working interests across gross wells/acreage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — productive wells (Item 1208(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Productive wells include producing wells and wells mechanically capable of production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count both currently producing wells and those mechanically capable of production as productive wells for reporting purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — undeveloped acreage (Item 1208(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Undeveloped acreage encompasses those leased acres on which wells have not been drilled or completed to a point that would permit the production of economic quantities of oil or gas regardless of whether such acreage contains proved reserves. Do not confuse undeveloped acreage with undrilled acreage held by production under the terms of the lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this operational definition to distinguish undeveloped acreage from other categorizations tied to lease terms or production status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — adequate geological evidence (mining)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate geological evidence, when used in the context of mineral resource determination, means evidence that is sufficient to establish geological and grade or quality continuity with reasonable certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this standard when classifying indicated resources and applying modifying factors for mine planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — conclusive geological evidence (mining)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusive geological evidence, when used in the context of mineral resource determination, means evidence that is sufficient to test and confirm geological and grade or quality continuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to measured resources and higher-confidence evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — cut-off grade
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut-off grade is the grade (i.e., the concentration of metal or mineral in rock) that determines the destination of the material during mining. For establishing 'prospects of economic extraction,' the cut-off grade distinguishes material deemed to have no economic value from material deemed to have economic value. Other similar terms include net smelter return, pay limit, and break-even stripping ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cut-off grade selection affects resource/reserve classification; justify choice relative to economic extraction prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — development stage issuer/property (mining)
rubrics_metrics.description: A development stage issuer is an issuer engaged in the preparation of mineral reserves for extraction on at least one material property. A development stage property is a property that has mineral reserves disclosed but no material extraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for categorizing issuer/property stage for disclosure obligations under the mining subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — economically viable (mining)
rubrics_metrics.description: Economically viable, when used in the context of mineral reserve determination, means that the qualified person has determined, using a discounted cash flow analysis, or has otherwise analytically determined, that extraction of the mineral reserve is economically viable under reasonable investment and market assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate economic viability via DCF or equivalent analytic methods using reasonable assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — exploration results
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploration results are data and information generated by mineral exploration programs that are not part of a disclosure of mineral resources or reserves. A registrant must not use exploration results alone to derive estimates of tonnage, grade, and production rates, or in an assessment of economic viability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploration results alone cannot support resource/reserve estimates or viability assessments; further studies are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — exploration stage issuer/property
rubrics_metrics.description: An exploration stage issuer is an issuer that has no material property with mineral reserves disclosed. An exploration stage property is a property that has no mineral reserves disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to classify company/property for disclosure thresholds and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — exploration target
rubrics_metrics.description: An exploration target is a statement or estimate of the exploration potential of a mineral deposit in a defined geological setting where the statement or estimate, quoted as a range of tonnage and a range of grade (or quality), relates to mineralization for which there has been insufficient exploration to estimate a mineral resource.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploration targets are conceptual ranges only and reflect insufficient data to declare resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — feasibility study (mining)
rubrics_metrics.description: A feasibility study is a comprehensive technical and economic study of the selected development option for a mineral project, including detailed assessments of all applicable modifying factors and detailed financial analysis necessary to demonstrate at the time of reporting that extraction is economically viable. It must be more comprehensive and accurate than a pre-feasibility study and include designs sufficient for investment decisions or project financing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feasibility studies are high-confidence, 'bankable' technical/economic studies required to support major financing or investment decisions; equivalent terms include full, final, comprehensive, bankable, or definitive feasibility study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — final market study (mining)
rubrics_metrics.description: A final market study is a comprehensive study to determine and support the existence of a readily accessible market for the mineral. At minimum it must include product specifications based on final testing, supply and demand forecasts, historical prices for preceding five or more years, estimated long-term prices, competitor evaluation, customer evaluation of product specifications, market entry strategies or sales contracts, and justification for all assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final market studies underpin feasibility conclusions and must document and justify market assumptions and contract/marketing plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — indicated mineral resource
rubrics_metrics.description: An indicated mineral resource is that part of a mineral resource for which quantity and grade or quality are estimated on the basis of adequate geological evidence and sampling; the level of certainty is sufficient to allow a qualified person to apply modifying factors in sufficient detail to support mine planning and evaluation of economic viability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicated resources may be converted to probable mineral reserves but have lower confidence than measured resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — inferred mineral resource
rubrics_metrics.description: An inferred mineral resource is that part of a mineral resource for which quantity and grade or quality are estimated on the basis of limited geological evidence and sampling. The level of geological uncertainty is too high to apply relevant technical and economic factors useful for evaluation of economic viability; inferred resources may not be considered when assessing economic viability and may not be converted to a mineral reserve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inferred resources are the lowest confidence category and cannot be used to support reserve declarations or viability analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — initial assessment (mining)
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial assessment is a preliminary technical and economic study of the economic potential of all or parts of mineralization to support the disclosure of mineral resources. It must be prepared by a qualified person, include assessments of reasonably assumed technical and economic factors, and demonstrate that there are reasonable prospects for economic extraction. It is required for disclosure of mineral resources but cannot be used as the basis for disclosure of mineral reserves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial assessments support resource-level disclosure but are insufficient for reserve classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — investment and market assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Investment and market assumptions include all assumptions about prices, exchange rates, interest and discount rates, sales volumes, and costs necessary to determine the economic viability of mineral reserves. The qualified person must use a price for each commodity that provides a reasonable basis for establishing that the project is economically viable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumptions must be reasonable and documented; commodity price assumptions should justify viability conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — limited geological evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited geological evidence means evidence that is only sufficient to establish that geological and grade or quality continuity are more likely than not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to classification thresholds below 'adequate' or 'conclusive' evidence levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — material (as used in mining disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Material has the same meaning as under § 230.405 or § 240.12b-2 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply general SEC materiality standards when determining whether mining operations or properties are material to the registrant's business or financial condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — material of economic interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Material of economic interest includes mineralization, including dumps and tailings, mineral brines, and other resources extracted on or within the earth's crust. It does not include oil and gas resources resulting from oil and gas producing activities, gases (e.g., helium and carbon dioxide), geothermal fields, and water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this scope when identifying what counts as mineral material for resource/reserve determinations under the mining subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — measured mineral resource
rubrics_metrics.description: A measured mineral resource is that part of a mineral resource for which quantity and grade or quality are estimated on the basis of conclusive geological evidence and sampling, sufficient to allow application of modifying factors in sufficient detail to support detailed mine planning and final evaluation of economic viability; a measured mineral resource may be converted to a proven mineral reserve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highest-confidence resource category suitable for direct conversion to proven reserves with appropriate modifying factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — mineral reserve
rubrics_metrics.description: A mineral reserve is an estimate of tonnage and grade or quality of indicated and measured mineral resources that, in the opinion of the qualified person, can be the basis of an economically viable project; specifically, it is the economically mineable part of a measured or indicated mineral resource, including diluting materials and allowances for losses that may occur when the material is mined or extracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserves must be founded on measured/indicated resources and a qualified person's opinion on economic mineability including diluting/loss allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — mineral resource
rubrics_metrics.description: A mineral resource is a concentration or occurrence of material of economic interest in or on the Earth's crust in such form, grade or quality, and quantity that there are reasonable prospects for economic extraction. It is a reasonable estimate of mineralization, taking into account relevant factors such as cut-off grade and likely mining dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources represent potentially extractable mineralization under assumed technical and economic conditions and are not mere inventories of drill intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — modifying factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifying factors are the factors that a qualified person must apply to indicated and measured mineral resources and then evaluate in order to establish the economic viability of mineral reserves. These include, but are not restricted to: mining; processing; metallurgical; infrastructure; economic; marketing; legal; environmental compliance; plans, negotiations, or agreements with local individuals or groups; and governmental factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and treatment of modifying factors depend on the specific mineral, mine, property, or project; they determine conversion of resources to reserves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — preliminary feasibility study (pre-feasibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary feasibility study is a comprehensive study of a range of options for the technical and economic viability of a mineral project that has advanced to a stage where a qualified person has determined a preferred mining method (underground) or pit configuration (surface) and an effective processing and sales plan. It includes financial analysis based on reasonable assumptions and is more comprehensive than an initial assessment but less than a full feasibility study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-feasibility supports decisions about conversion potential and is intermediate confidence between initial assessment and feasibility study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — preliminary market study (mining)
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary market study is sufficiently rigorous to determine and support the existence of a readily accessible market for the mineral, including product specifications based on preliminary testing, supply and demand forecasts, historical prices, estimated long term prices, competitor evaluation, customer evaluation of product specifications, and market entry strategies. It must justify all assumptions but can be less rigorous than a final market study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for early-stage market assessment supporting pre-feasibility studies or resource disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — probable mineral reserve
rubrics_metrics.description: A probable mineral reserve is the economically mineable part of an indicated and, in some cases, a measured mineral resource.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents a reserve classification that follows indicated resources, with lower confidence than proven reserves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — production stage issuer/property (mining)
rubrics_metrics.description: A production stage issuer is an issuer that is engaged in material extraction of mineral reserves on at least one material property. A production stage property is a property with material extraction of mineral reserves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to determine disclosure obligations and categorization under the mining subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — proven mineral reserve
rubrics_metrics.description: A proven mineral reserve is the economically mineable part of a measured mineral resource and can only result from conversion of a measured mineral resource.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highest-confidence reserve category; conversion requires measured resource and application of modifying factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — qualified person
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualified person is an individual who is (1) a mineral industry professional with at least five years of relevant experience in the type of mineralization and type of deposit under consideration and in the specific type of activity that person is undertaking on behalf of the registrant; and (2) an eligible member or licensee in good standing of a recognized professional organization at the time the technical report is prepared. For an organization to be recognized it must meet criteria such as being reputable, admitting members primarily on academic qualifications/experience, establishing professional standards, requiring continuing professional development, having disciplinary powers, and providing a public list of members in good standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualified person criteria include minimum experience and professional organization membership; registrants must ensure and document that persons meet these qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — relevant experience for qualified person
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant experience means experience in the specific type of activity the person is undertaking for the registrant (e.g., exploration, resource estimation, reserve estimation), and may require experience with specific deposit types, sampling/analytical/extraction/processing techniques, and application of modifying factors as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant experience is a facts-and-circumstances determination; related deposit-type experience can count. For technical reports, relevant technical-method experience is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: General instruction — scope of 'mining operations' and when disclosure is required (§229.1301)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mining operations include operations on all mining properties that a registrant owns or has/probably will have an economic interest in, operates or likely will operate under lease or legal agreement, or has/probably will have associated royalty or similar rights. A registrant must provide the disclosure specified in the mining subpart if its mining operations are material to its business or financial condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing materiality consider quantitative and qualitative factors in the context of the registrant's overall business; aggregate operations across properties and include related activities from exploration through extraction to first point of material external sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: General instruction — presentation, glossary, and plain English (§229.1301(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: When providing summary or individual property disclosure, the registrant should provide an appropriate glossary if technical terms are used; should not include detailed illustrations and technical reports, full feasibility studies, or other highly technical data in the filing (though such materials must be furnished supplementally upon request); and should use plain English principles to enhance readability for investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accessible explanations, glossaries for technical terms, and avoid embedding overly technical materials in public filings; maintain availability of technical reports to staff on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified person and technical report summary — reliance and responsibility (§229.1302(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant's disclosure of exploration results, mineral resources, or mineral reserves must be based on and accurately reflect information and supporting documentation prepared by a qualified person. The registrant is responsible for determining that the person meets the qualified person definition and that the disclosure accurately reflects the qualified person's information. If multiple qualified persons are relied upon, the registrant's responsibilities apply to each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants must vet qualified persons, ensure accuracy of reported information, and maintain supporting documentation for each qualified person engaged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical report summary — content, signature, and filing requirements (§229.1302(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant must obtain a dated and signed technical report summary from the qualified person that identifies and summarizes the information reviewed and conclusions reached about the registrant's mineral resources or mineral reserves on each material property. If more than one qualified person prepared the summary, each must date and sign and clearly delineate sections prepared by each. A third-party firm of experts may sign instead of naming individual employees. The technical report summary must be filed as an exhibit when disclosing mineral reserves/resources for the first time or when there is a material change from the last filed summary; similar filing rules apply for exploration results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure signed, dated technical report summaries are prepared and filed as exhibits when required; delineate contributions when multiple qualified persons are involved; third-party firm signatures are acceptable under specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical report summary — exceptions for royalty/streaming companies (§229.1302(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that has a royalty, streaming, or other similar right is not required to submit a separate technical report summary for a property that is covered by a current technical report summary filed by the producing mining registrant; it may refer to the producing registrant's filed technical report summary (reference will not be deemed incorporation by reference absent an express statement). A registrant lacking access to the technical report summary because obtaining it would be an unreasonable burden/expense or a request for it was denied need not file a summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Royalty/streaming registrants may refer to producing registrant's filed summaries; document inability to obtain summary if relying on the exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified person consent and disclosure of employment/affiliation (§229.1302(b)(4)-(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant must obtain the written consent of the qualified person to use the person's name, or any quotation from or summarization of the technical report summary, and to file the technical report summary as an exhibit. If multiple qualified persons prepared the summary, obtain written consent from each. If a third-party firm signed, the firm must provide consent; if the qualified person is an employee or affiliated with the registrant, the person must provide consent individually. For Securities Act filings, the written consent must be filed as an exhibit; for Exchange Act reports, the consent need not be filed but should be retained. The registrant must state whether each qualified person is an employee; if not, name the employer and disclose any affiliation or interest and describe the nature of any affiliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure and retain written consents as required and disclose employment/affiliation information for non-employee qualified persons in the filing.
